description: Reproduction attempt of the 'Vibrato strength' unsupervised-editing example (PC #3) from the AudioLDM2 unsupervised zero-shot editing method (ZEUS), as shown on the project page https://hilamanor.github.io/AudioEditing/ and Figure 4(b) of the paper (arXiv:2402.10009). This run uses the site's exact 8-second demo clip, with no spectral mask applied.

source.reference_example: docs/index.html row 4, 'Various Samples (PC direction changes)' table, label 'Vibrato strength'

input_audio.identity: MedleyDB MusicDelta_Gospel excerpt, 8-second clip as used on the project page
input_audio.preprocessing: converted mp3 -> wav, 16kHz mono 16-bit PCM via ffmpeg (required: audioldm.utils.get_duration uses Python's stdlib wave module, which cannot read mp3)

model.source_prompt: A recording of ryhtmic clapping, a women singing, and drums and guitar playing.
model.prompt_source: verbatim from docs/index.html row 4 'Inversion Prompt' column (typo 'ryhtmic' preserved as-is, since it is what was actually used and affects the text embedding)

commands.step1_pc_extraction: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python main_pc_extract_inv.py --init_aud MDDBGospel_8secs.wav --model_id cvssp/audioldm2-music --source_prompt "A recording of ryhtmic clapping, a women singing, and drums and guitar playing." --results_path pc_extractions --drift_start 150 --drift_end -1 --n_evs 3

key_parameters.note_on_evals_pt: repo default (--evals_pt ./eigvals.pt) points to a dataset-averaged eigenvalue file the repo never ships; patched main_pc_apply_drift.py line 31 default from './eigvals.pt' to None so it falls back to the extraction's own per-timestep eigenvalues (the behavior the README describes as 'leave --evals_pt empty', which the actual `is not None` check in the code does not achieve with an empty string)

environment.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti, 16GB VRAM (Blackwell, sm_120)
environment.note: repo requirements.txt does not pin torch/transformers/diffusers/huggingface-hub; the repo is 2024-era code and the default latest versions of these (as of this run, e.g. transformers 5.16.1, diffusers 0.40.0, huggingface-hub 1.29.0) are mutually incompatible with each other and with this codebase's assumptions. Versions above are what was pinned to get a working environment; see pip_freeze_working_env.txt for the complete resolved set.

runtime.extraction_iteration_rate: ~9.7 sec/iteration for the ~150 PC-extraction timesteps (drift_start=150 covers almost the full 200-step trajectory)

outputs.orig.wav: true source clip, re-synthesized: mel-spectrogram extraction + HiFi-GAN vocoding of the raw input (not byte-identical to the source mp3, but a faithful reference)
outputs.reconstruction_noPC.wav: sanity-check baseline: DDPM-inverted then regenerated with the SAME source-prompt conditioning and ZERO drift applied. Tests inversion fidelity independent of any PC edit.
outputs.extraction_spectrogram.png: mel-spectrogram of reconstruction_noPC.wav, auto-saved by main_pc_extract_inv.py
outputs.corrs.png: diagnostic: cosine-correlation of each PC's eigenvector between consecutive extraction timesteps (for PC 1/2/3). Values stayed near 0 (not near +-1) throughout, meaning PC identity is not stable across timesteps in this run -- this is the reason the method freezes a single timestep's direction (use_specific_ts_pc) rather than trusting a per-timestep-varying direction.
outputs.MDDBGospel_pc3_a2.wav: PC #3 applied with amount=+2 (frozen at t=120) across drift range [150,-1]
outputs.MDDBGospel_pc3_a-2.wav: PC #3 applied with amount=-2 (same direction, opposite sign)
outputs.analysis_output.txt: full stdout of analyze_vibrato.py (pitch/F0, vibrato-band oscillation, harmonic/percussive energy split, spectral diff between a2/a-2)

finding.hypothesis_tested: Does this independently-re-extracted PC #3 reproduce the paper's 'vibrato strength' effect?
finding.verdict: NOT CONFIRMED -- measured evidence points to an instrumental/percussive-balance change rather than an isolated vocal vibrato change.
evidence: percussive_frac_of_total (harmonic/percussive RMS split): orig=0.558, reconstruction_noPC(baseline)=0.562 (consistent) vs a2=0.628, a-2=0.805 -- large, direction-dependent swing toward percussive/rhythmic content

median F0: orig/recon_noPC/a2 all ~83Hz (consistent) but a-2 jumps to ~294Hz (~2 octaves) -- inconsistent with a singer's fundamental simply gaining vibrato; suggests the pitch tracker is latching onto a different/altered harmonic source

spectral diff between a2 and a-2: the 15 largest per-frequency-bin differences are almost all under 200Hz (bass/kick-drum/low-guitar range), not the 300-3400Hz vocal formant range where vibrato would concentrate
likely_causes: no --seed fixed, so the independently-run power-iteration eigendecomposition likely converged to a different 3rd principal direction than the paper's original run
corrs.png shows PC identity is inherently unstable across timesteps even within this single run; freezing t=120 does not guarantee landing on whatever the paper's PC #3 represented
significant library-version drift (2024-era diffusers/transformers/torch vs. this run's versions) can shift the numerics of a higher-order eigenvector
next_steps_if_pursuing_vibrato_specifica: rerun with a fixed --seed for reproducibility across attempts
extract more PCs (raise --n_evs) and screen each with the same analysis script rather than trusting the index number
try the masked run (patch=[128,256], covering ~5-10s) -- confining extraction to a specific segment may isolate a cleaner direction; see ../run2_16sec_masked_pc3/ once complete
